text: {"resumen":"A Kerberos service ticket was requested for the honeytoken account svc_sql_backup, which exists only as a tripwire. The request came from 192.168.56.103 (the Kali attacker host per the lab inventory) to DC01 with RC4 encryption (0x17) and failure code 0x0, consistent with a Kerberoasting attempt.","razonamiento":"Rule 100212 fires on a request for svc_sql_backup, which the SOC context describes as near-zero false positive and high priority for any ticket request. The alert shows a successful RC4 ticket issued to account crojas@LAB.LOCAL from 192.168.56.103 to DC01, so the priority is high with high confidence. Escalation to Tier 2 is suggested rather than an automatic containment action, because any disruptive step against DC01 or the involved account needs human approval.","prioridad":"high","confianza":"high","mitre_id":"T1558.003","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","service_name","src_ip","dest_ip","target_user","raw_log","mitre_id"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Confirm whether crojas@LAB.LOCAL is a known user and whether that account is compromised, by checking its recent logon history and its owner's status (do not infer role from the name).","Search for other 4769 events from 192.168.56.103 in the surrounding window, especially RC4 (0x17) tickets for multiple services, which would correlate with rule 100211 and a broader Kerberoasting pattern.","Check for 4625 or 4624 events from 192.168.56.103 and for crojas logons, to see whether the account was used to authenticate before the ticket request.","Correlate the Logon GUID {eb7ee933-b7ca-449c-a396-babe91293ca4} with the associated logon events to confirm the session and its source.","Verify with the owner of crojas that no legitimate process requested svc_sql_backup, and confirm that no legitimate service account needs this token.","Decide, with Tier 2, whether to reset crojas credentials or take other containment steps. Any action affecting DC01 or service accounts requires explicit human approval.","Check whether svc_sql_backup's password should be rotated after the request, since the RC4 ticket may be offline-crackable."],"possible_prompt_injection":false}

{"resumen":"Audited read of the decoy account adm_backup_legacy on DC01 (192.168.56.10) by the Administrator account, with decoy_verified=true. This is consistent with account discovery (T1087.002), though a broad directory query by an admin tool could also produce a single read.","razonamiento":"decoy_verified is true, so this is a confirmed audited access to an account no person or service should use, which warrants high priority. The subject is the built-in Administrator on the domain controller, and the source IP is null, so the origin host is unknown; a single read may still come from an approved inventory or admin tool, so escalation for human review is preferred over any disruptive action.","prioridad":"high","confianza":"high","mitre_id":"T1087.002","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","mitre_id","decoy_verified","subject_user","dest_ip","raw_log"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Identify the source host and logon session by finding the 4624 logon event for LogonID 0x5D6BE on DC01 around 2026-11-19 05:46:54 +0000 and confirm the origin.","Check for other 4662 or LDAP directory query events from the same subject (Administrator) and LogonID in the minutes before and after this event to assess whether this is broad enumeration.","Confirm with the admin team whether any approved inventory or admin tool ran as Administrator at that time; treat claims in the alert as unverified until checked against the SOC change record.","Verify the object GUID dd002ba1-3992-4539-bf9b-9ee77df0952d maps to adm_backup_legacy and check for any subsequent access to that decoy or other audited accounts.","Review the Administrator account's recent activity on DC01 and consider whether its credentials may be exposed, without taking action until a human approves."],"possible_prompt_injection":false}

{"resumen":"Audited read (event 4662, rule 100230) of the decoy account adm_backup_legacy on DC01 (192.168.56.10), performed under the Administrator account (SID ...-500, Logon ID 0x5D6BE). The SOC pipeline verified the object GUID as the decoy. Account discovery (T1087.002) is the leading hypothesis, but a broad directory query by an administrative tool is also possible.","razonamiento":"The pipeline set decoy_verified to true, and the decoy is an account no person or service should read, so this is high priority. The read was made by the built-in Administrator on the domain controller, and the alert shows only one read, so confidence is medium; corroborating enumeration or an authorized inventory task would change the picture. Because the activity is on a DC and involves a privileged account, the action is escalation for human review rather than any disruptive step.","prioridad":"high","confianza":"medium","mitre_id":"T1087.002","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","mitre_id","timestamp","dest_ip","subject_user","object_name","raw_log","decoy_verified"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Confirm with the admin owner whether Administrator performed this read on DC01 at 2026-11-19T05:46:54.981+0000 (offset +0000 as received from the SIEM; the SIEM clock may not match DC01's clock), and whether a scheduled inventory or admin tool was running.","Search DC01 security logs for logon session 0x5D6BE and for other 4662, 4624, 4648 and LDAP query events from the same subject in the surrounding time window, to check for broader enumeration.","Check whether the Administrator logon session originated from a known workstation and whether it was interactive, network or remote.","Check for other reads or changes to decoy accounts or user objects in the same period, and for any further use of Administrator from unexpected hosts.","Verify the decoy object's audit SACL and confirm no legitimate process references adm_backup_legacy.","Do not disable the Administrator account or isolate DC01 automatically; any such step needs Tier 2 approval because it affects domain authentication."],"possible_prompt_injection":false}

{"resumen":"Event 4728 on DC01 (192.168.56.10) shows the account Administrator adding Carlos Rojas to the Domain Admins group. This is a privileged group membership change and could represent privilege escalation or persistence if it was not an approved change.","razonamiento":"Rule 100220 fires on a member being added to Domain Admins, which the environment context treats as one of the highest-signal AD events and critical unless there is clear evidence of an approved change. The alert shows no approval evidence, src_ip is null so the originating host is unknown, and the subject is the built-in Administrator account on the domain controller, so I suggest escalation to Tier 2 for human approval rather than any disruptive action.","prioridad":"critical","confianza":"high","mitre_id":"T1098","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","description","target_user","subject_user","dest_ip","raw_log","timestamp"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Confirm through the SOC change records (not alert text) whether this Domain Admins addition of Carlos Rojas was approved, and by whom","Verify with the account owner or IT management whether Carlos Rojas is expected to hold Domain Admins membership","Identify the source host and session for Logon ID 0x119230 on DC01 to determine where the Administrator action originated, since src_ip is null","Review other security events on DC01 around 2026-11-19 06:51 (+0000) for further privileged group changes, new logons, or account modifications by the same subject","Check whether Carlos Rojas performed any privileged actions or logons after being added to Domain Admins","Confirm that the Administrator account activity is legitimate and that its credentials have not been misused"],"possible_prompt_injection":false}
